recognize_zh: 放大後的痰液抹片可見一條 S 形彎曲、身體均勻細長、尾端漸細的線蟲幼蟲，體內可見細顆粒狀內部構造，位於淡藍色黏液團中；痰液中出現此種幼蟲符合糞小桿線蟲（Strongyloides stercoralis）的播散性感染。
features: Single S-shaped nematode larva with uniform slender body, rounded anterior end and tapering posterior end
Purple-staining body with granular internal cellular structure and visible cuticle outline
Larva embedded in a pale blue mucoid/fibrinous aggregate
Tail tip morphology (notched vs pointed) and esophageal length not definitively resolvable
describe_en: Higher-magnification view of a sputum cytology preparation shows an S-shaped nematode larva with a slender, uniform body, rounded anterior end, tapering posterior end and granular internal structure, lying within a pale mucoid aggregate. The background contains sparse inflammatory cells. Fine anatomic features used for speciation, such as the notched tail of filariform larvae or the short buccal cavity of rhabditiform larvae, are not clearly resolved in this image. Findings are consistent with Strongyloides stercoralis larva in sputum, indicating pulmonary involvement and possible hyperinfection syndrome.

ddx.vs: Filariform hookworm larvae have a pointed tail and rhabditiform larvae a long buccal cavity, whereas Strongyloides filariform larvae have a notched tail and rhabditiform larvae a short buccal cavity with prominent genital primordium.
Microfilariae are narrower, often sheathed, and show a column of discrete nuclei with species-specific tail nuclei, typically in blood rather than sputum.
Ascaris larvae are larger and occur only during early pulmonary migration, often with marked eosinophilia and Löffler syndrome.
